hankel_image — MATH transform op

• Data kinds: image2d → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.hankel_image(image, *, center=None, spacing: 'float' = 1.0, n: 'int' = 256, r_max: 'float | None' = None) -> 'dict' (to call the implementation directly, import mathtransforms; mathtransforms.hankel_image(image, *, center=None, spacing: 'float' = 1.0, n: 'int' = 256, r_max: 'float | None' = None) -> 'dict'; from the registry, opsmath.get("hankel_image"))

Usage

Obtains the 2-dimensional Fourier transform of an axisymmetric image (a round aperture, a Gaussian blob, diffraction rings) with 1 radial Hankel transform.

The image is split into rings 1 pixel wide by distance from the centre and averaged (radial profile), then passed to hankel_transform (order 0). If axisymmetric, the 2-D transform takes just 1 integral (averaging over rings also reduces noise by 1/√(pixels per ring)), and how far it departs from axial symmetry is returned as a number (asymmetry). The frequency step is about 1/(2·radius), as with the 2-D FFT; it does not get finer.

Args:

image: 2-D real image.

center: centre (row, col). If omitted, the brightness centroid.

spacing: length of 1 pixel (sets the frequency unit).

n: number of samples of the Hankel transform.

r_max: upper limit of the radius used (default = shortest distance from the centre to the image edge; rings with missing corners are not used).

Returns:

nu (frequency), F (radial cross-section of the 2-D Fourier transform, the value of ∬ f e^{−2πi k·x} dx), r, profile (radial profile),

center, asymmetry = ‖image − axisymmetric image rebuilt from the profile‖ / ‖image‖ (0 means axisymmetric; not diluted by a dark background).

Gate: a disc of radius R gives F(ν) = R J₁(2πνR)/ν (Airy), exp(−π r²/σ²) gives σ² exp(−π σ² ν²) (self-dual scaling), and it matches the radial cross-section of the 2-D FFT.

Family-wide input contract (fail-closed)

Every mathops op validates its input before computing (nothing slips through silently):

• complex input raises ValueError — coercing to float64 silently discards the imaginary part (numpy only emits a ComplexWarning and returns a plausible-looking wrong real number). State .real/.imag/abs() explicitly, or use complexops, which handles complex data.

• masked arrays with masked elements raise ValueError — the implicit conversion that peels off the mask and uses the raw values underneath is refused. Say explicitly whether to fill or to drop.

• NaN/Inf raises ValueError on every input (refused with the count stated — it propagates through the whole result).

• Shapes are strict: 1-D and 2-D are never implicitly promoted or broadcast (a matrix in a vector slot, or a vector in a matrix slot, raises ValueError; reshape explicitly).

• Size cap: ops that take a matrix, and the stat_histogram bins, raise ValueError beyond mathops.MAX_ELEMENTS (2^26 ≈ 67 million elements).
